agree.reason: The pilot arithmetic and the June checkpoint are persuasive, but the ad-background members are left with blanks exactly where they will push hardest: why not run both, how the gap is funded, what happens to the sales colleague, and how many pilot members are still paying.

honest.reason: The memo rightly softens the 'replace within a year' claim, but it calls the $47,000 drop a decline over 'two years' at 'about 20% a year' and says ads 'fell two years running', which misstates a single one-year fall of 36%.

works_the_facts.reason: The membership figures are well derived and check out (about $20,000 a year from the pilot, 875 members needed, 55 a month needed against roughly 150 a month already reached, about 540 by June), but the ad trend is smoothed into a weaker form when the true 36% one-year fall would strengthen the case.

right_comparison.reason: The no-change alternative is projected at $67,000 for 2027 from a wrongly annualised 20% decline; if the actual 36% fall continued, ads would bring in about $54,000, which nearly erases the stated $12,000–$29,000 gap.

qualification.reason: The checkpoint has a date (June 30), an expected count (about 540), a trigger (under 450, still bracketed) and a consequence (return to the board in July with options, including sponsorships), though the gap-funding hedge is still an unfilled placeholder.

objections.reason: The memo names the right objections (the revenue gap, why not run ads and membership side by side, the 11-year colleague) but answers the side-by-side and colleague questions only with placeholders, and it understates how fast ads are declining, which is the strongest reply to the ad-background members.

fit.reason: It is a tight, one-page board memo with a clear decision request, though it has several unfilled placeholders, some of them substantive.
